one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window. First, Q3 2026 results, which NXP investor relations confirms for Oct 27, 2026 at 4:10 PM ET (call 4:30 PM), so the first reaction is Oct 28. Second, the FOMC decision on Oct 28 at 2:00 PM ET, following the 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16. The Q3 guide is $3.75B revenue and $4.11 EPS. Management said at Goldman Sachs on Sep 9 that pricing and lead times are building, so a beat is likely. The swing factor is the Q4 guide against the ~$4.3 implied consensus, plus any comment on distributor sell-in: Q2 distribution revenue grew 26.7% y/y against 9.4% for direct, and channel inventory is 11 weeks versus 9. The Q2 beat still sold off, and the last two earnings weeks moved +21% and -15%, so I do not take a directional view. The median is ~$237.5, a hair above spot for the expected beat, and the sigma is ~13.5% for the month (48%/3.5 plus an earnings gap and a same-week FOMC). The Oct 8 dividend has no ex-date in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of $19.0 x 14x = $266; and FCF yield (40%): 2027 FCF/share $15.2 at a 6.0% yield = $253. Blended ~$261, rounded to $260. Both the multiple and the yield were tightened for the Sep 16 Fed hike.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Sep-2027 (Q4'27-Q3'28) $19.0 x 14x forward P/E

inputs_detail.input: FY2025 non-GAAP EPS (base of 2030 EPS-doubling ambition)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $18.10-18.13, grown ~10% into 2028 (consistent with management's aim to double EPS from $11.81 by 2030, a ~15% CAGR), gives a Q4'27-Q3'28 run-rate of ~$19.8. I haircut it ~4% for peak-cycle pricing and channel risk, and I keep the haircut at 4% after re-checking the 10-Q. China is $630M of $3,496M (18%) of Q2 revenue, so China car retail at -20.8% YTD alone cannot move group EPS much. But distributor revenue rose 26.7% y/y against 9.4% for direct sales, and it is 59% of revenue, which is the broader sell-in risk. Result: $19.0.

The stock trades at ~13.1x the $18.10 2027 consensus today and was ~19x at $300 in June (TIKR). In round 1 I used 15x. I cut it to 14x because the Fed raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026, its first hike since 2023, and more hikes are projected. A hiking cycle historically caps cyclical-semi multiples. 14x still allows a small re-rating from 13.1x as the 2027 margin targets (60% GM, 34-40% OM) are reached.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue $15.88B x 24% FCF margin = $3.81B / ~250M shares = $15.2 FCF/share, capitalized at 6.0%

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026 FCF margin 22.6% and FY2025 19.8%. Capex runs ~2-3% of revenue, but VSMC/ESMC JV capacity fees and equity injections continue (Q3: $70M fees + $80M VSMC + $30M ESMC). With operating leverage at higher revenue, 24% is plausible
252.2M shares outstanding on July 24, 2026 and 254M diluted in the Q3 guide. Buybacks slowed ($104M in Q2), so assume only ~1% net reduction

At $236.47 the 2027 FCF yield is ~6.4%, and at the $300 June price it was ~5.1%. Round 1 used 5.75%. I raise it to 6.0% because the Sep 16 hike lifts the risk-free rate by 25bp with more hikes projected. It also reflects cyclicality and ~$7.75B of net debt (1.5x).

bear.story: The 2026 upturn proves partly sell-in. Distribution (+26.7% y/y in Q2 versus +9.4% direct) and China (+25.5% y/y while China car retail is -20.8% YTD) unwind as channel inventory above 11 weeks is worked down. Price increases reverse, and Fed hikes pressure cyclical multiples. FY27 EPS lands near $15 and the stock trades at ~11x NTM, near its March 2026 trough.

base.story: NXP delivers roughly consensus: 2026 EPS ~$15 and 2027 ~$18. Gross margin moves toward 59-60% and data center/physical-AI ramps begin. With rates rising, the multiple recovers only to ~13.5-14x a ~$19 NTM EPS.

bull.story: Pricing sticks, lead times keep extending, and the channel build proves to be end demand. Revenue beats the 2027 plan, GM exceeds 60% and NTM EPS reaches ~$21. The multiple re-rates to ~16.5x despite the Fed, above the $340 May high but short of the June 19x peak.

thesis_break_reason: $175 is below the 52-week low ($183) and ~9.7x the $18.10 2027 consensus EPS. At that level the market would be discounting an earnings reset to ~$14-15 FY27 EPS. Likely causes: a distributor/China sell-in unwind (distribution +26.7% y/y against direct +9.4%, channel inventory 11 weeks versus 9 a year ago), pricing reversal, an export-control shock, or a rate-driven cyclical downturn. Any of these would contradict management's no-restocking statements. Moves between $200 and $230 are ordinary for a stock with ~47% realized volatility (the May-August $340-to-$229 drawdown happened while fundamentals were rising).

Durability of price increases versus the historical low-single-digit annual price declines

reasoning: Round 2. The primary documents still show fundamentals accelerating: Q2 2026 revenue was $3.50B (+19.5% y/y), non-GAAP GM 58.0% and EPS $3.61, and the Q3 guide is $3.75B / $4.11. 2027 consensus EPS of $18.10-18.13 is still being revised up, and the stock trades at ~13.1x it. The supervisor made two findings I missed, and I confirmed both from primary sources. First, the Fed raised rates to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (Fed implementation note). Second, China revenue is +25.5% y/y but only 18% of revenue, and China car retail is -20.8% YTD. Re-reading the 10-Q, I found a more important channel signal than the China q/q figure: distributor revenue rose 26.7% y/y against 9.4% for direct sales, and it is now 59% of revenue. That is the real pull-in exposure. It is larger than China but still not proof of restocking at 11 weeks of channel inventory. On the rate hike, I cut the P/E multiple from 15x to 14x ($266) and raised the FCF yield from 5.75% to 6.0% ($253). The blended fair value falls from $275 to $260. The scenario mean is ~$258 (bear $165/0.25, base $258/0.5, bull $350/0.25). I set the ladder median at ~$250, below the mean because of the negative skew of cyclical earnings. It uses a lognormal with 45% sigma, near the 47% trailing weekly realized volatility (45% over 13 weeks), so I no longer argue that realized was inflated by the April spike. I added slightly more left-tail mass for a channel unwind. As the supervisor asked, I trimmed the far right tail (P>=591 from 2.9% to 2.2%): it needs NTM EPS of ~$25 at ~24x, which a hiking cycle makes less likely. I still keep more upside tail than a thin-tailed view, because the stock ran from $191 to $340 in two months this year. P(>=spot) is 0.55, down from 0.57. I ignore Ambarella in valuation (unconfirmed, small) and treat it as a catalyst only.
